h: וַיֵּלֶךְ וְשַׁבָּת תְּשׁוּבָה, ט׳ Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah, 9
"Take Words with You": Lesser Teshuvah and the Dew of Torah

p: A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day:
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem"
and in the Pesikta it is stated:
"But one who confesses and forsakes shall find mercy"
וּבִפְסִיקְתָּא הַחֲדָשָׁה (פְּסִיקְתָּא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא כד, יח)
And in the Pesikta Chadashah (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana 24:18),
did you not come with words?
(and so they said in Bamidbar Rabbah 7:4).
But it is difficult to say this
about the Stand at Har Sinai,
where they put "we will do" before "we will hear,"
as one man with one heart;
when they heard the utterance "I am"
Torah learning was implanted in their heart,
and when they heard "You shall have no"
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their heart.
that about this it is said
and with their tongue they lied to Him"
along the lines of what they said
even though the yetzer hara was uprooted from them
at the time of Matan Torah,
so it is already called a lie,
and this is "and with their tongue they lied to Him."
"And they were not faithful in His covenant"
in light of what is said,
and since it later returned to its place
it says, "and they were not faithful in His covenant."
of one whose mouth and heart are not alike,
but of one who for the moment
nevertheless at the time of the act
he is called a baal teshuvah.
on condition that I am a tzaddik,
even if he is a complete rasha,
for perhaps he thought of teshuvah.
And this implies that we see him
still conducting himself in his wickedness,
he has certainly turned from his evil.
If so, what does it mean
that he will never return to this sin,
to forsake his wickedness and return,
even though his yetzer later overpowered him
and he went back to his ways,
which speaks of the lesser teshuvah,
"for you have stumbled in your iniquity"
as referring to teshuvah from fear,
through which deliberate sins become for him like unintentional ones.
and the difference between unintentional and deliberate
and this is nullified through speech,
and only the deed alone remains;
therefore they become for him like unintentional sins.
that He carry away the iniquity entirely;
"Bring us back in complete teshuvah before You";
for it is from Hashem Yisbarach
to help that the teshuvah be
that the teshuvah be complete, out of love;
"I will be like the dew to Yisrael"
"For Your dew is a dew of lights"
whoever makes use of the light of Torah,
the light of Torah revives him;
whoever occupies himself with the dew of Torah,
the dew of Torah revives him.
with which He will in the future revive the dead
and it is the aspect of the Dew of Atika,
which is the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
"My speech shall drip like the dew"
which alludes to Torah she'b'al peh,
how it comes down from Heaven
"For in much wisdom is much anger"
This is what the pasuk says:
and strike his roots like the Levanon";
and this follows what they said
"In days to come Yaakov shall take root,
these are the talmidei chachamim in Bavel
who make buds and blossoms for the Torah.
for in Bavel was the main
through the Men of the Great Assembly,
This is what they said in the Midrash
at Sinai they acted with their mouth
"They beguiled Him with their mouth," etc.;
in Bavel they acted with their heart
and did not act with their mouth,
that at Sinai they acted with their mouth
and the yetzer hara returned to its place;
and this is "they lied to Him,"
through the Men of the Great Assembly,
who abolished the yetzer for idolatry
and this is that they acted with their heart,
for it was uprooted from the heart forever;
for with their mouth they promised
of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh;
for the dew of Torah she'b'al peh
is effective to repair the "much anger."
and it is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
that a great man says a thing
and it is then reported in the name
that the yetzer hara be uprooted
that he will not return to this sin
with the help of Hashem Yisbarach.
as it is stated in the holy Zohar
"On this day the head is filled —
and casts it upon the Field
and especially at the second meal,
which is the meal of Atika,
as they said in the holy Zohar there —
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem":
"I will be like the dew to Yisrael,"
and the yetzer hara will be uprooted
And this is the power of teshuvah
that became known to Adam HaRishon,
and he stood up and said,
"A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day:
it is good to give thanks to Hashem."
May Hashem complete matters for us for the good,
and bring us back in complete teshuvah before You.

Rabbi Yehudah said: Was it not with words that you beguiled Him at Sinai — 'They beguiled Him with their mouth, and lied to Him with their tongue' (Tehillim 78:36)? paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 2:2 — "And what is teshuvah? That the sinner abandon his sin, remove it from his thoughts and resolve in his heart never to do it again, as it says, 'Let the wicked abandon his way' (Yeshayahu 55:7); and also regret the past…; and He Who knows hidden things will testify about him that he will never return to this sin."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86b — "Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like unintentional ones, as it says, 'Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity' (Hoshea 14:2)… But Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like merits, as it says, 'And when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, on account of them he shall live' (Yechezkel 33:19)! There is no difficulty: here, from love; there, from fear."

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 88b — “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: With every utterance that came from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel departed, as it is said, ‘My soul departed when He spoke.’ If their souls departed at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead in the future and revived them, as it is said, ‘You showered abundant rain, O God; when Your inheritance was weary, You sustained it.’”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 11 — “And about this it says, ‘My speech shall drip like the dew,’ which is the aspect of the Oral Torah, which is like dew: it is not seen as it falls, but only from what we see afterward, that the earth is moist, is it recognized that dew fell. So too the Oral Torah: it seems to a person that he is innovating the words of Torah, but in truth they are the words of the living God.” Connection: Both read “My speech shall drip like the dew” as the Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 145b; Rashi, s.v. She’einan bimkoman — “Why do the Torah scholars of Bavel distinguish themselves by their appearance? Because they are not in their own place. As people say: 'In my town, my name; outside my town, my clothing.' Rav Yosef taught concerning the verse 'Those who come shall take root in Yaakov; Israel shall blossom and flower': These are the Torah scholars of Bavel, who produce blossoms and flowers for the Torah.” Rashi explains “not in their place” as meaning that they were exiled there from Eretz Yisrael, and explains the proverb: in one’s own city one is recognized by name, whereas in a foreign place one’s clothing supplies the public distinction. This is Rabbi Yochanan’s answer, correcting the earlier suggestion that the dress compensates for a lack of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Pirkei Avot 1:1 — “Moses received Torah from Sinai and transmitted it to Joshua; Joshua to the elders; the elders to the prophets; and the prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly. They said three things: Be deliberate in judgment, raise up many students, and make a fence for Torah.” The transmission culminates in the assembly whose program Rav Tzadok invokes: the expansion of students and the protection of Torah through a fence.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 88a — “Rabbi Abba said: Blessing is prepared for those supernal days, which are blessed from this day. On this day the head of Zeir Anpin is filled with dew descending from Atika Kadisha, the most concealed of all. He pours it upon the field of holy apples three times from the entrance of Shabbos, so that all will be blessed together.” The threefold flow of dew is the specific basis for linking the three Shabbos meals to the upper and lower modes of receiving blessing.
